papers.title: Some complete $\omega$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
papers.abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $\Sigma^\omega$ in $\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k$, and by $\checked{D}_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $\Sigma$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $\omega$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\in\Sigma^\omega\mid\forall i\in\omega ~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $\checked{D}\_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0\_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k>3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbf{\Delta}^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].

papers.title: Finite-on-Top-of-Temporal CSPs in Fixed-Point Logic
papers.abstract: We study definability in fixed-point logic with counting (FPC) for a class of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) that simultaneously generalises finite-domain CSPs and temporal CSPs. The templates for the CSPs are first-order expansions of the structure $([k] \times {\mathbb Q};<_1,\dots,<_k,\sim)$ where $<_i \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid x<x'\}$ and $\sim \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid i \in [k], x,x' \in {\mathbb Q}\}$, i.e., $k$ copies of $({\mathbb Q};<)$. Such a CSP is definable in FPC precisely when the template pp-constructs neither the ternary temporal relation $X$, which holds on three elements if the minimum is attained exactly twice, nor a nontrivial finite affine structure. Equivalently, the template has global polymorphisms that witness the tractability of the temporal CSPs on the copies, and that provide 3-4 weak near-unanimity operations on the set of copies of ${\mathbb Q}$. In this case, we prove that the CSP is even expressible in the less expressive logic FP$^*$, which is the restriction of FPC without counting terms (i.e., the extension of first-order logic by a fixed point operator and an ordered auxiliary number sort). Our algorithm samples finitely many values in each copy and then performs nested constraint-singleton consistency tests (which is a uniform polynomial-time algorithm for finite-domain CSPs). The correctness proof uses finite-domain CSP theory to combine consistency certificates by a single polymorphism term, fixing each variable to one copy without destroying the certificates needed for the temporal algorithm. We then use a known normal form for algebraic products to control the remaining interactions between different copies.

papers.title: Internal Languages for Thin Epsilon-Hyperdoctrines: Soundness, Completeness, and Rocq Formalization
papers.abstract: We present a typed proof-term calculus for intuitionistic intensional first-order logic with Hilbert's epsilon-operator and prove its soundness and completeness with respect to hyperdoctrinal models with thin bicartesian closed setoid categories (BiCCCs) as fibres and formula-indexed witness selections. The calculus provides an explicit internal language for these epsilon-hyperdoctrines: for each fixed typed signature, its syntactic term model is initial for syntax-indexed, interpretation-preserving model morphisms, with uniqueness up to setoid equality. The nested epsilon syntax is organized by a well-founded dependency relation on formula labels. Concrete countermodels exhibit failure of excluded middle and show that formula conversion need not identify the selected witnesses. We also compare the full calculus with its epsilon-free and epsilon-only fragments. The principal constructions and metatheorems are formalized in Rocq. With setoid BiCCCs, proof irrelevance is a choice of equality, not the erasure of proofs: the proofs and their categorical operations remain available as the basis for a future proof-relevant categorical semantics.

papers.title: A characterization of the finite model property for $\omega$-categorical theories
papers.abstract: A first-order theory $T$ has the {\em finite model property} if every first-order sentence that is implied by $T$ has a finite model. We give a characterization of when a complete $\omega$-categorical theory $T$ has the finite model property. The characterization makes it possible to transfer stability theoretic results in [29] to certain classes of finite structures. This approach also gives information concerning properties that a sequence of finite ``base structures'' of ever larger size must have in order for its random expansions to a larger vocabulary to have a chance to satisfy a convergence law for first-order logic.

papers.title: A Nullstellensatz for the field of complex Laurent series
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be the theory of the valued field of complex Laurent series $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$ in the language of rings expanded by a constant for $t$ and by predicates for $n$-th powers. We introduce a $t$-adic analogue of Kochen's operator, namely $\gamma(x)=x/(1+tx^{2})$, and the associated Kochen ring $\Lambda_{L}$ of a field extension $L$ of a model $K$ of $T$. Our main result characterizes the field extensions of $K$ which embed into a model of $T$ (the formally $T$-adic} fields): $L$ is formally $T$-adic if and only if $1/t\notin\Lambda_{L}$. As an application we prove a Nullstellensatz for $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$: a polynomial $f\in K[X_{1},\dots,X_{n}]$ vanishes on the zero set of an ideal $I$ if and only if $f^{m}=\sum_{i}\omega_{i}f_{i}$ for some $m\geqslant 1$, generators $f_{i}$ of $I$ and coefficients $\omega_{i}$ in the ring $\Lambda_{K(X)}\cdot K[X]$. We derive the resulting correspondence between $R$-ideals and algebraic sets, and we compare natural incarnations of the associated $T$-spectrum: prime ideals, morphisms into models of $T$, and the space of types of $T$.

papers.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
papers.abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.

papers.title: Ramsey properties of trees and $C$-relations via the partite construction
papers.abstract: Finite convexly ordered binary branching $C$-relations have been viewed as a notable exception to the broad applicability of the partite construction in structural Ramsey theory. The absence of a proof of their Ramsey property by the partite construction was noted by Bodirsky in his 2015 survey and pointed out again by Hubi\v{c}ka and Kone\v{c}n\'y in their 2026 survey. We overcome this limitation by giving proofs based on the partite construction of the known Ramsey properties of the class $\mathcal{CT}$ of finite convexly ordered treeable meet semilattices and of the classes of finite convexly ordered $C$-relations with arbitrary branching and with binary branching. Our proofs do not rely on Milliken's tree theorem. The key is to expand $\mathcal{CT}$ by level predicates and a predecessor function so that the locally finite subclass method applies. We then transfer the resulting Ramsey witnesses to the corresponding reduct classes and to the classes of convexly ordered $C$-relations.

papers.title: High-Arity Rademacher Complexity and Uniform Laws of Large Numbers
papers.abstract: We characterize several properties of higher-arity function classes, specifically finite $\VC_k$-dimension, slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension, and finite slicewise Littlestone dimension, in terms of generalizations of Rademacher complexity. These characterizations sets up simple new proofs of several results on finite $\VC_k$-dimension and slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension. These include the preservation of finite $\VC_k$-dimension under taking expectations and uniform law of large numbers statements for both properties. All of these results apply naturally to real-valued function classes as well as boolean-valued classes. We also prove a new adversarial uniform law of large numbers for classes with finite slicewise Littlestone dimension.

papers.title: Chain Continuity and Scott-Closed Interpolation
papers.abstract: We prove that every chain-continuous dcpo is continuous and that its way-below relation is the relational square of its chain-below relation, answering a question of Ern\'e. A subalgebra lattice obtained from a locally finite J\'onsson algebra shows that the chain-below relation itself need not interpolate. For approximation by Scott-closed sets, we give a finite-upper-bound characterization on lower-set lattices and characterize interpolation by an extension property for directed lower sets. This yields a countably based, completely distributive algebraic lattice on which chain and directed approximation coincide, whereas Scott-closed approximation fails to interpolate, answering questions of Ern\'e and of Ho and Zhao.

papers.title: Remarks on ultrafilters exponentiation
papers.abstract: Recently, two exponentiations of ultrafilters have been introduced in [7]. We rephrase them in nonstandard terms, and use the nonstandard formulations to characterize some of their properties. We also study their relations with divisibility by introducing factor-picking functions and highly exponential ultrafilters.

papers.title: Tight $\sigma$-filtrations and the BFPP of $C(\omega^*)$
papers.abstract: Assuming that $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$ is tightly $\sigma$-filtered, we prove that $C(\omega^*)$ fails the ball fixed point property. This axiom holds under the continuum hypothesis and in the $\aleph_2$-Cohen model. The proof shows that the Stone space of the countable--cocountable algebra $\operatorname{Cc}(\omega_1)$ is a continuous retract of $\omega^*$ and uses the equivalence between tight $\sigma$-filteredness of $\operatorname{Cc}(\omega_1)$ and of $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$. We also prove that the quotient of a tightly $\sigma$-filtered Boolean algebra $B$ with the countable separation property by an $\aleph_1$-generated $P$-ideal is a Boolean retract of $B$.

papers.title: Controlling The Skips of Arithmetic Sets
papers.abstract: Andrews, Ganchev, Kuyper, Lempp, Miller, A.\ Soskova, and M.\ Soskova conjectured that skip-cototality coincides with weak cototality. We show that the conjecture is false by constructing a $\Pi^0_2$ set whose skip does not have a cototal degree. We further adapt this construction to obtain additional results. We prove that for each odd $n$, there is a $\Pi^0_{n+1}$ degree whose $n$-iterated skip does not have a cototal degree. We show that there is a $\Pi^0_2$ degree which does not contain an introenumerable set.

papers.title: Order-preserving maps of the Turing degrees: regularity and consistency strength
papers.abstract: We formulate a proof of Part~I of Martin's conjecture for order-preserving maps directly on the quotient of the reals by Turing equivalence. The assumptions are countable choice for reals, the perfect-set property for sets of reals, and continuous uniformization on a comeager domain. The argument applies under $\mathsf{AD}+\mathsf{DC}_{\R}$ and inside the choiceless Solovay model. We then determine the exact consistency strength of the unrestricted order-preserving dichotomy as an axiom over $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{AC}_{\omega}(\R)$: it is equiconsistent with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ plus a strongly inaccessible cardinal.

papers.title: A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $\sigma$-Complete Embedding
papers.abstract: We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $\sigma$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $\pi_a\pi_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.

papers.title: Nonstandard combinatorial ultrafilters and a new local witness model
papers.abstract: A central object in the theory of proof complexity generators is Krajicek's local witness model. We construct a new such model as a definable ultrapower using a definable version of a selective ultrafilter over a model of arithmetic. We transfer some set theory of combinatorial ultrafilters to the definable nonstandard setting.

papers.title: A counterexample to Vaught's Conjecture for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$
papers.abstract: We construct a sentence of $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ having exactly $\aleph_1$ many countable models up to isomorphism, but no perfect set of non-isomorphic models. This disproves Vaught's conjecture for infinitary logic. The construction follows a framework devised by Robin Knight, and the proof has been formally verified in Lean.

papers.title: Teams, Truthmakers, Translations
papers.abstract: We present a faithful translation from Aloni's logic BSL into a classical modal logic over semilattices combining ideas from earlier modal translations of truthmaker semantics with algebraic representation theory. We show how our method can also be made to work for other current hyperintensional logics. Finally, we place our results in a broader setting of translating hyperintensional logics into classical modal ones, and discuss applications and new challenges that arise for both areas of philosophical logic connected in this way.

papers.title: Baire measurable functions and automorphisms of the truth-table degrees
papers.abstract: We show that if an automorphism $\pi$ of the truth-table degrees is induced by a Baire measurable function $F\colon 2^{\omega}\to 2^{\omega}$, or merely induced on some comeager set by a continuous function, then $\pi$ is the identity. The same results hold for the weak truth-table degrees. The argument is an adaptation to truth-table reducibility of OpenAI's recent proof that the Turing degrees are rigid.

papers.title: Proper varieties of distributive l-pregroups are periodic
papers.abstract: We show that every proper variety of distributive $\ell$-pregroups is periodic; as a result, the subvariety lattice of the variety of distributive $\ell$-pregroups decomposes into a disjoint union of bounded intervals each consisting of all properly $n$-periodic varieties, for different $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. On the way, we study non-periodic (one-generated) subalgebras of $\mathbf{F}(\mathbb{Z})$ and show that they either contain a non-periodic idempotent or they contain idempotents of arbitrary big periodicity. The same results holds for non-periodic one-generated subalgebras of $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{J} \overrightarrow{\times} \mathbb{Z})$, where $\mathbf{J}$ is a chain, generated by a composite element and the resulting idempotents can be taken to be local in the associated wreath product.

papers.title: Linear Logic via algebra I: Girard algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop several aspects of the algebraic theory of Girard algebras, regarded as the equivalent algebraic semantics of multiplicative additive Linear Logic $\mathsf{MALL}$. The main structural results concern the bottom of the subvariety lattice of the variety of Girard algebras: varieties generated by simple Girard algebras generated by the constants correspond exactly to the atoms of the lattice. Moreover the lattice itself is atomic, i.e. every nontrivial subvariety contains an atom. These atoms can be represented uniformly by the maximal filters of the free algebra generated by the constants. Moreover every congruence of this free algebra is realized by a subvariety, and the resulting atom-support topology records the behavior of arbitrary joins: the atoms below a join of atoms are precisely the points in the closure of the corresponding subset of the spectrum. The concrete constructions show that the bottom of the lattice is already quite rich. Besides determining the integral and degenerate boundary cases and exhibiting finite modular and nonmodular atoms and chains of covers, we constructed infinite families of atoms whose topology reflects genuinely infinitary behavior; thus finite and infinite joins behave essentially differently at the bottom of the subvariety lattice. On the logical side, these results yield $2^{\aleph_0}$ Post-complete extensions of $\mathsf{MALL}$.

papers.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
papers.abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.

papers.title: Functional Projection and Complexity Reduction
papers.abstract: T\"ornquist (arXiv:1310.3250) proved that if there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_2$ maximal almost disjoint (MAD) family, then there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$ MAD family. Since then, several other "complexity reduction" proofs have been found for other combinatorial objects, such as maximal independent families or ultrafilters. All of these proofs have relied on $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$-uniformization, so they did not easily lift to higher projective levels. In this paper, we introduce a principle weaker than Uniformization which we call "Functional Projection", and show that this principle is sufficient for most complexity reduction proofs. On the other hand, we prove that in $L[U]$, the canonical inner model for a measurable cardinal, Functional Projection holds for $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ relations. As an immediate corollary, we obtain that in $L[U]$ there are $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ witnesses for many combinatorial families.

papers.title: Fragments of SRP, the nonstationary ideal, and diagonal reflection
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationships between fragments of SRP and diagonal reflection principles. It turns out that the subcomplete fragment of SRP, augmented with CH, implies that the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$ is not saturated, but that Larson's diagonal reflection principle $OSR_{\omega_2}$ holds. In contrast, it was known that the full principle SRP implies the saturation of the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$, but it does not imply $OSR_{\omega_2}$. We find several instances of this phenomenon: pairing (variations of) the subcomplete fragment of SRP with stronger failures of the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$ to be saturated allows us to conclude more instances of diagonal reflection principles, while boosting (the corresponding variations of) the full principle SRP with strong forms of the saturation of the nonstationary ideal allows us to produce models where these principles still hold, yet weaker versions of diagonal reflection fail.

papers.title: On separable pairs of fields and beautiful pairs of separably closed valued fields
papers.abstract: We continue the study of beautiful pairs of henselian valued fields, initiated in joint work of the second author with Cubides Kovacsics and Ye. As our main result, we show that separably closed non-trivially valued fields of arbitrary imperfection degree admit beautiful pairs which are elementary pairs satisfying certain natural axioms. They satisfy beauty transfer, i.e., saturated models of their theory are again beautiful. The same holds for beautiful pairs associated to natural subclasses of all definable types, most notably for all definable types orthogonal to the value group and for all bounded definable types. This yields strict pro-definability of the space of the definable types from any of these classes, in the theory SCVF of separably closed non-trivially valued fields. We also show a separable analog of a classical result of Keisler's, namely that the first order theory of an infinite separable extension $L/K$ of fields - considered in the pairs language and where the large field $L$ is separably closed, is determined by the theory of the small field $K$ together with the imperfection degree of $L$ over $K$.

papers.title: Model theory of quasitracial $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras and the absoluteness of monotone completeness
papers.abstract: We examine various applications of logic to $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras, particularly the monotone completeness conjecture. We develop a model theory for $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras equipped with a faithful normalized quasitrace. Using this language, we provide a separable coding which allows us to reduce the finite case of the monotone completeness conjecture to monotone sequential completeness of $\mathrm{II}_1$ $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factors. Combining an explicit recursive axiomatization with the completeness theorem for continuous logic, we show that this case of the conjecture, and Kaplansky's problem whether every $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ is a von Neumann algebra, are each equivalent in ZFC to a $\Pi^0_2$ sentence of arithmetic, so that their answers are the same in every $\omega$-model of ZFC. We also consider real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras. Here the Baer-$*$-ring notion of an abelian projection must be distinguished from commutativity; following the real-operator-algebra terminology we call the former semi-abelian. Handelman's matrix theorem implies that a real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebra with no nonzero central semi-abelian projection has $\mathrm{AW}^*$ complexification. We answer a number of other open problems in real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras.

papers.title: Failure of the strong feasible disjunction property
papers.abstract: A propositional proof system $P$ has the strong feasible disjunction property iff there is a constant $c \geq 1$ such that whenever $P$ admits a size $s$ proof of $\bigvee_i \alpha_i$ with no two $\alpha_i$ sharing an atom then one of $\alpha_i$ has a $P$-proof of size $\le s^c$. We combine the work of Ilango (2025) and Ren et al. (2025) with the gadget proof complexity generator of K. (2007) and rule out the property for strong enough proof systems under the following two hypotheses: - there exists a language in class E that requires exponential size circuits even if they are allowed to query an NP oracle, - there exists a P/poly demi-bit in the sense of Rudich (1997).

papers.title: Optimizing Proof-Search via Linearization for G\"odel-L\"ob Logic with Tree-Hypersequents
authors: Omar Y. A. A. Taher (TU Dresden
papers.abstract: We answer a question posed by Poggiolesi concerning a syntactic decidability proof for GL in the tree-hypersequent system CSGL, and resolve a challenge identified by Maggesi and Perini Brogi, who sought a PSPACE proof-search algorithm for GL in expressive sequent-based formalisms. We work with a notational variant of CSGL formulated in terms of (labeled) tree sequents. Our answer is complexity-optimal: we present a proof-search algorithm that decides the (in)validity of formulae and runs in PSPACE, matching the known PSPACE-completeness of GL. To achieve this, we introduce a "linearization method", which constructs only a single branch of a derivation and of a tree sequent at a time, avoiding the exponential blowup typical of naive proof-search in sequent formalisms. We show how to systematically combine fragments of tree sequents generated during proof-search to extract finite counter-models, which serves as a theoretical device for establishing the correctness of the algorithm when proof-search fails. Finally, we show that every valid formula admits a proof consisting solely of line sequents, which correspond to linear nested sequents. This establishes a connection between depth-first proof-search and linear nested sequent calculi. Our results not only answer the aforementioned questions, but also provide new insights into proof-search and correctness arguments in tree sequent systems for modal logics.

papers.title: Proofs Without Nominals: G\"odel's Ontological Argument, its Shallow Embedding, and the Open Questions of the Monatshefte Notes
papers.abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzm\"uller and Scott's Notes on G\"odel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument, reaches beyond the modal object language: its property quantifiers range over domains containing the nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic. A proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding, not necessarily of the modal logic. That the framework affords this is not new. Whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled by replaying it in an explicit calculus, one result at a time. More cheaply, and for all results at once, it can be approached by analysing what the embedding's proofs substitute. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof in the embedding substituting nothing outside the object language: 294 of them explicit proofs, machine-checked, none using a nominal. The Notes' own proofs substitute none either; what the check flags are terms a prover introduced. The three questions the Notes leave open are settled too, without nominals, but by the empty instance of the conjunction axiom, too cheaply to convince. As the Notes generalise it, to cover G\"odel's "any number of summands", the axiom covers the empty conjunction and the singleton. This article restricts it to at least two different conjuncts, a non-degenerate reading of G\"odel's footnote, and settles the questions again, without nominals. In effect the restriction excludes only the empty conjunction; the one-element case comes back with the other axioms. In one of the three variants the restriction refutes the possible existence of a God-like being; the answers return, with no side condition, once the Notes' non-emptiness clause is confined to G\"odel's essence. Every theorem stated here is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4; the countermodels are Nitpick's, checked by the build.

papers.title: G\"odel Implication on Finite Chains: Catalan Enumeration and a Continuum Limit Law
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of output values produced by all fully bracketed implication terms on $n$ distinct variables in G\"odel $m$-valued logic on the finite chain $V_m$. The Catalan decomposition of bracketings yields a stratified system of recurrences for the output counts. Passing to tail sums reduces this system to a finite iteration of a single map $\Phi_x$ and its inverse branch $\Psi_x$. For each fixed $m$, this reduction gives a common dominant square-root singularity at $r=1/(4m)$, coefficient asymptotics of order $(4m)^n n^{-3/2}$, and limiting proportions for every truth level. In the four-valued case these proportions are obtained explicitly in nested radicals. The main new phenomenon appears when the number of truth values also tends to infinity. If $K_m$ denotes the output level under the limiting $n\to\infty$ distribution and $X_m=K_m/(m-1)$, then $X_m\Rightarrow X$, where $X$ has density $(1+2t)^{-3/2}$ on $[0,1)$ together with an atom of mass $1/\sqrt{3}$ at $1$. In particular, the top mass converges to $1/\sqrt{3}$, while the bottom mass is asymptotic to $1/m$. We further show that the same probability law arises intrinsically when G\"odel implication is defined directly on $[0,1]$ and valuations are sampled from Lebesgue product measure: the continuum tail generating function satisfies an exact first-order differential equation whose critical specialization is the ODE appearing in the finite-chain Euler limit. We also record a root-split refinement whose pair-count generating functions factor as products of the level generating functions and inherit the same square-root scale.

papers.title: Beth companions of finitary essentially algebraic theories
papers.abstract: For categories, being balanced (meaning that every arrow that is both epic and monic is an isomorphism) can be regarded as a strong tameness property which plays an important role, for example, in algebra and logic. We study the problem of associating a balanced companion category, called a \emph{Beth companion}, to a locally finitely presentable category (equivalently, the category of models of a finitary essentially algebraic theory). We show that, if it exists, the Beth companion is unique and can be described in terms of \emph{saturated} objects. Under additional assumptions, we prove that Beth companions can be computed as orthogonality classes, and admit a syntactic presentation via Gabriel--Ulmer duality. Furthermore, we establish conditions for the transfer of properties from a category to its Beth companion. A number of examples of categories that do or do not admit a Beth companion are provided. In particular, we show that the category of commutative rings does not admit a Beth companion, and employ Pierce sheaf representations to describe the Beth companion of other classes of rings.
